q: What goes into the CBAM figure for ferrochrome from an Aktobe or Aksu smelter?
title: Kazakh ferrochrome: the CBAM figure
short: Direct emissions from the carbon in coke, coal and electrodes, plus any fuel burnt for pre-heating or drying, worked out by mass balance and divided by tonnes of alloy. Power from Kazakhstan's coal plants is indirect and not charged for ferro-alloys, though steel buyers will ask for it separately.
audience: Ferrochrome producers in Aktobe and Pavlodar regions and EU stainless mills buying from them

ul: Coke and coal used as reductant in the electric furnaces.
Fuel for chrome ore pellet sintering or pre-heating kilns, if inside the installation.
Carbon leaving in alloy, slag and dust.

p: High carbon ferrochrome is declared under 7202 41 and other ferrochrome under 7202 49. Both are iron and steel goods, charged on direct emissions.

sections.h: What a stainless mill will add
p: Electricity per tonne, because the coal heavy grid makes it the largest share of the product footprint even though CBAM leaves it out.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas and electricity invoices and production records into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so the direct emissions behind each tonne can be traced to the documents. Emissions factors outside India are entered from the official source and labelled.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
